I bought Ozmafia!! for two reasons: the artwork is gorgeous and the story sounded interesting. I'm glad I did, because I honestly enjoyed this game more than I thought I would. It had a few issues for me, but overall my experience in the game was pleasant. Since I try to end things on positive notes, I'll start with the bad.
(For this review, I use the herione's default name of Fuka)
- While the majority of the music was very nice, that jingle during the scene transition quickly got on my nerves. You can turn it off, but doing so means turning off the sound effects which was fine for me in the end, but some people might not want to lose all of them.
- Having more options is usually never a bad thing, but I feel like they wanted so many character routes but didn't have time to really flesh them all out? The Oz boys, of course, have the most in terms of story-content, but on the flip side you have characters like
and Caesar, who felt very rushed? The first more so than the second, honestly.
- I'm sure someone out there liked the Brothel and Robin Hood routes, but I honestly could not stand them. The Brothel route, had it just been a developing romance between Fuka and Manboy (or even Alfani) would have been fine, but Dorian just ruined it for me. True, you can choose options that lead to Fuka willingly staying, but the whole route just left me very uncomfortable. Now Robin Hood's route, oh boy, let me tell you I was super frustrated when I realized where it was heading. Which was early on because they did not seed the 'surprise' of this route very well.
Listen, I'm all for 'person loses someone they love and mourns them but are able to find love again' because it's realistic; there's no rule saying that just because you love one person, you can't love another, but dude Robin Hood just, I mean look, there is mourning the loss of a loved one and then there is Robin Hood's method, which was to
.
His whole route could have been the hurt/comfort trope and it would have been fine, hell his desire for vengeance could have still factored in, but the way it turned out was just disgusting. In one of his endings, I didn't get the sense that he really loved Fuka—he was just settling for her, since
, and in the other, well he doesn't love her at all and so she becomes a nun. And the best part of all this? It doesn't matter which ending you're going for, because he's still going to show up at Fuka's cottage, ask her to tell him if she loves him, then
.
- I'm pretty sure this feature was used as a way of appealing to a replay, I wasn't fond of how certain scenes could only be accessed during second playthroughs. It's not a huge deal, because I had to go back through some of the routes anyway for CG's but, it leads into my last issue with the game...
- The pacing. The story for this game is interesting, I'm a sucker for fairytale's and reimagining them, but the pacing for this game is so weird. Like I said above, a lot of extra scenes are unlocked only if you replay a route, but that means on your first time through, you're going to be left wondering why a scene ended suddenly and why when the next begins, it seems like a lot of time has passed. Even with the extra scenes, it doesn't help too much in some areas (like fight scenes), and it's sad because I feel like if they had done a better job with that, then this game would have been even better.
- Fuka's amnesia is literally never resolved in any of the routes. It's constantly talked about, but nothing comes of it until the epilogue and grand finale, which while I enjoyed both, are locked behind objectives: to get the epilogue, you must see at least one ending from every route. To get the grand finale, you must see ALL endings for all the routes AND you'll need to watch the epilogue. This was annoying because it meant I had to go through routes I'd rather not have (the Brothel and Robin Hood ones especially), but thankfully the game offers a skip mode. Both the epilogue and grand finale have nothing to do with the romance routes, btw.
- The artwork is absolutely gorgeous. It was also nice to have a little avatar of Fuka, showing her expressions during her speech and such. I'm disappointed that she wasn't voiced during the main game, because when you hear her voice in the epilogue and grand finale, it's so adorable.
- Despite the choppy pacing, the story was interesting. It's obviously heavily focused on the story of Dorothy and her time in Oz, but I felt like the spin they put on it was really good.
.
- Even though some of the routes were disappointing, like the ones I mentioned above, I did enjoy a vast majority of the ones offered and even some of the NPC's. I liked how so many fairytale characters were reimagined and their personalities were very different (Hansel and Gretel were hilarious, btw). The Oz guys were all great, and I had a hard time choosing one I liked more, though I think Kyrie wins for me; I have a thing for characters like his, and after viewing the epilogue and grand finale, it feels like his has the most involvement in the overall story. Caramia was super sweet and Axel was adorable. Scarlet's route would have earned more points if I felt like they took the romance aspect more seriously, and Soh was also a character who took me by surprise! I definitely recommend giving him a shot, because his endings are emotional and he, like Kyrie, has a deeper connection to the overall plot.
- Caesar was also a surprise; he spends most of the game as the 'bad guy' but it's easy to see when he shows up more that he's not nearly as threatening as he makes himself out to be, and his romance was adorable; I have a thing for gruff guys who are secretly soft and affectionate. He has a lot of interactions with Soh, so I liked that as well!
- I had to follow a guide to get the Transfer Endings, which are essentially you start romancing one guy, but wind up with another. These are only available for the Oz guys (Caramia, Kyrie, and Axel). When you're playing and going for one of them, another will usually fall for Fuka and that will result in a love triangle. You can either reject them by going along with the route for the guy you want or, if you pick different answers, you can decide to leave the first guy and choose the second. The reason I list this under a positive is because the game handles this choice relatively well. It's obvious that it hurts the guys, but Fuka also goes through some guilt over it, but when it's all over and the choice is made, all of them act like adults. Plus, some of the transferred endings are actually nicer than the Pure Love endings--Kyrie's transfer ending A was, in my opinion, absolutely adorable and I kind of consider that my 'canon' route. Caramia and Axel's were nice as well, but I have a bias for Kyrie I think.
Overall, the game was worth the price for me and I hope they release the other's over here, because I'd definitely like more Ozmafia!! content to play.

This has become one of my favorite otome games, hands-down.  An easy recommendation to fans of otome VNs!
Ozmafia is a visual novel with many choices to make and several different endings.  The gameplay consists entirely of reading and making those choices - there are no stats or time management in this one.  The description on the store page is very accurate as far as the story goes, so I will not bother to recap it here.  Suffice it to say, this is an extremely well-done visual novel and worth the full price!  Buying Ozmafia gets you a wealth of content: There are 10 characters with routes, and multiple paths in each one.  Each character has a minimum of 2-3 significantly different endings, with some having as many as 4-6 (can't remember the exact total count).  Unlike in some VNS where the main plot stays the same and your route only affects extra scenes, each of the 10 characters' routes significantly changes the events your character experiences.
The characters themselves are some of my favorite in any otome game, and the different paths allow you to explore different sides and possibilities to the characters.  Each of the "main" three characters, especially, are quite deep, and their personalities are very well fleshed-out.  In one of my favorite routes, the player's choices can either temper or feed into the route character's insecurities, and the way he expresses himself changes a lot as a result.
The art is consistently beautiful (as you can tell from the screenshots), both the regular sprites and the CGs (of which there are plenty).  Even in other visual novels with above-average art, I rarely find myself visiting the CG gallery after completing a character's route; in Ozmafia, however, I was often drawn back to ogle the scenes.  (I would say this game is a tad spicier than the average otome -- nothing goes past PG-13, but that is still a lot more than most otome games, which treat a tap on the shoulder as a super scandalous event.)  Furthermore, the voice-acting is top-notch (which is evident even if you do not speak a word of Japanese), and the voices fit the characters wonderfully.  Again, 100% recommended!

First off, as the opening theme at the top of the page demonstrates, the music is great. The art too, is fantastic. (Fun fact: The artist is the same for Diabolik Lovers, another great Otome from Otomate). The interface is cute, but not overly done. The atmosphere and setting is well-established, and the characters are quite charming. The MC, Fuka, is also cute, but could be rather ignorant and clueless in some (if not most), situations. Although that isn't necessarily her fault.
However, it's also important to note that a couple of routes contain trigger warnings. OZMAFIA!! is a fun game, but some routes and characters are likely to creep you out and dart into rather dark themes. Something to also consider is that the final epilogue of this game is actually only accessible once you complete every route and ending OZMAFIA!! has to offer. So this could be a bit of a turn-off to those that wish to avoid such themes.
Also, be sure to SAVE OFTEN. Replaying routes is necessary to complete the CG gallery and obtain all the endings. So the ability to load save files at the route's turning point is a huge convenience as well as a time saver, (or unless you're like me and insist on seeing the extra scenes that are available upon repeated playthroughs from start to finish... which I still consider an annoyance, as those scenes could've easily been included in the first playthrough, and saving the player many hours of playtime).
OZMAFIA!! is a flawed game, and not a perfect one by any stretch of the means, but it has great art, a cute soundtrack and a plot interesting enough to keep the player engaged. Although the game drags on at some points, OZMAFIA!!'s an experience worth considering for Otome and Visual Novel fans to play from the growing list on the Steam market.
If asked how I'd score it, I'd give a 7.5/10. Has holes, but none so big that it should be avoided from playing firsthand.

Ozmafia!! is a solid game. Good voice acting, graphics and story. The localization is pretty good too, which is my pet peeve. The characters are fairly distinctive, so there were some I really didn't like (Kyria) and others I loved (<3 Axel!!).
It's a little annoying that you have to replay every guy's route to see all the extra scenes, and that means you'll be using the skip function A LOT. But it also means there's more incentive to replay the stories and the game is detailed. Some parts of scenes aren't voiced so it's a little odd when the voices come in and out in scenes, but I'd rather have sporadic voice acting that's high quality like this than none, so I won't complain too loudly.
There were a few routes I didn't want to play so I didn't unlock all the secret bonus stuff :( but I think I got my money's worth and overall I'd recommend this game if you like falling in love with pretty anime guys.

I was finally able to play this game and the wait was very worth it!

The way the characters interact with each other is what I really love, especially with Japanese humor.  I've played Ceaser's route (the wolf) and I was dying with laughter.  I'm a huge comedy fan so when it's matched with romance, I adore it immensely.
The MC, known as Fuka, can be quite clueless but I find it pretty adorable.  I can see why she would take everything so literal since she lost her memories.   You could compare her with Amnesia: Memories' heroine, but I find that Fuka to be more dimensional but that's because the two games are different, the other having a spirit helping her without others knowing while Fuka already has someone watching over her (in this case, the Oz group).   Fuka can be pretty silly and ignorant to some things (especially with others teasing her), she does pick up on it though later so she's not completely clueless.
The full price is very worth it since the localization and artwork, CG, voicework, and story is very lovely so far.  I haven't gotten everything yet, but so far, I really like what I see.  I hope to see more otome games localized by MangaGamer.   Give it a shot when you can, no pun intended ;D

Outbreak The New Nightmare is a Resident Evil based zombie game where the players will play as survivors trying to fight for their lives against the zombie threat. This is a 4 player co-op game and its all about helping eachother because if you die just once in a match you can't respawn so you need to be careful on what way you fight the zombies. This game is just like Resident Evil because the game uses camera angles, an inventory system and a health system which is described as Fine, Warning, Caution, Poison or Danger.
Pros:
+ 6 characters with their own backstory, buffs, debuffs, stats and perks. Every one has their own stats that can be improved by gaining levels.
+ Many different scenerios to play on. (maps)
+ The game is not easy on single player so players will need to be smart to survive.
+ Teamwork is important in the game because you need teammates to support you with ammo or medical items, help you progress through the match you're playing on and prevent you from dying just once and have to spectate for the rest of the game.
+ the game is very challanging on higher difficulty levels! Even in Multiplayer!
+ You need to manage your limited inventory so you need to make decisions on what you take or leave.
+ 3 modes named Campaign mode which is the story, Onslaught mode which is an endless wave mode that gets harder the more players progress and Experiments mode which is other objectives and challanges.
+ It does not matter if someone elses kills an enemy and gets the xp for the kill. Everyone gets the xp everytime someone kills an enemy.
+ Different types of enemies players will encounter.
Cons:
- The game needs more popularity.
- The codes that are used for puzzles are not randomized and this will lead to players remembering the codes and easily progress to the next objective.
- The Ai needs to be improved a little bit. Zombies sometimes walk into doors that are locked until it is unlock by a player that uses a key or walk into a wall which can be easy targets for players.
- It needs more intense atmosphere and music to make it a horror game.
Right now l am enjoying this game and l do recommend it to people who have played Resident Evil or really enjoy zombie survival games. I've done this a few dozen times and still die instantly in the third area while using the fire magic that the forest enemies are weak against, I just have to do it another 100 times, spending hours and hours on this boring♥♥♥♥♥♥to be powerful enough like I did in the first area so I could survive the level 1 forest area. Its not even worth continuing to play it, theres just too many better games in my queue some of which were also <$1.
Not to mention free downloads of emulated old Gameboy games are about the same graphics and layout quality with the same style of gameplay but far better difficulty balance so its not so boring to play. Like with Pokemon RGB/Yellow you could actually beat the game with just your starter by defeating every enemy that you bump into naturaly and every trainer/gym leader with him and not do any training, or even do some training with multiple pokemon to work out strategies and its not as boring because you have mini goals (new moves, evolutions) where as in this game you get nothing from leveling except automatic health and power increase, doesn't even have the most basic of rpg strategy elements: stat/skill points to apply. Instead you gain skills by clicking on stuff in nature...
In say LoZ OoA/OoS for Gameboy you don't even have to deal with this stupid grinding♥♥♥♥♥♥because it doesn't have player levels its just based on your own skill as a player, but this game is like the opposite of that they have only very rudimentary strategy like use fire spell to damage willowosips or do more damage to elves, wind spell to do more damage to mosquitos in the first area. But by the time you are able to tolerate the level 1 forest area you have all of the best equip from the first town (except the lucky charm, which I have now and it does nothing) and can kill those mosqitos with one physical attack anyway. I was informed in the comments that despite the fact that I was prevented from entering the area to the north of the first area which is what forced me to enter the forest area second, the game is designed to allow the player to go to that area. After I bought "Legend of Mysteria RPG" which is developed by the same guy(s) I knew that this game and the sequel are going to be epic. So I waited for a sale and bought them both. These are the best 24 cents I've ever spent for a game (48 for the 2 of them). I got "Legend of Mysteria RPG" in a bundle for maybe 10-15 cents. Now, just because they are cheap doesn't mean they are bad. Personally I had a great time playing them. I will focus on reviewing my experience in "Labyronia RPG".
It's an RPG game (obviously) so that's a plus (for me at least). You fight monsters and bosses, get gold, eat food to regenerate hp or use spells to do that, gain xp, buy a lot of things, explore the map, collect key items, level up, collect cues to learn new spells. I love all of that!
I've followed two guides to complete the game. Yes, I died a lot of times and spent time wandering but my point is that it's not a short game.
The music is good (not irritating). At different areas it changes. I enjoyed one particular track and the rest were ok.
There are many characters, few of which are the main ones. Most of the game you will fight monsters with a single character.

It turns out that "Legend of Mysteria RPG" is connected to "Labyronia RPG". I mean, in the latter I've been to a place that I'd already visited in the former. However there were still a lot of new areas to explore and that's always been fun. Speaking of which, the map is huge. There are a lot of places to visit and it takes time to do so (I am not complaining).
The only drawback is that the game crashed twice. But I played it for 15 and a half hours so I can't complain. You have 16 save slots so save often.
There are achievements, all of which can be unlocked (I did that) and there are also trading cards (I don't care about them).
So for this price it's a must-buy. It's ridiculously cheap if you ask me. I've played tons of games which were more expensive and I didn't enjoy some of them as much as I enjoyed "Labyronia RPG". Can't wait to play the sequel. Great game for a great price. The "Add to Cart" button is waiting for you to click it. Don't hesitate and do that.

In my opinion the graphics look best when playing zoomed out in a window, rather than full screen (toggle using F5/F6). The soundtrack keeps things interesting and, at times, the music choices really add to the atmosphere of the scenes. The controls are also very simple to use.
The only downside I can foresee is that once the quests are complete, there is limited replay-ability. On the plus-side though, there is Labyronia 2 and Mysteria to follow.
At such a low price, Labyronia is really worth exploring.

"Timberman: All the fun of working in the firewood business without any of that boring getting paid for your labour or getting a reasonable price for your precious commodity crap to get in the way of the excitement of being a rejected character from a mildly amusing and slightly trans-phobic Monty Python sketch minus the catchy tune to distract you. When I was a child, as the eldest son chopping and bringing in the firewood was a chore I was assigned during the winter months. So believe me when I say I know that chopping wood is fundamentally chore-like. There's a reason why my Dad insisted that I take on this responsibility as soon as I was old enough to swing an axe. So as you might understand playing this game is extremely chore like.

And when played on a computer then it's nowhere near as good as when you play it on android.
So take my advice and get the Android version instead.

A Quiver of Crows is like someone tried to make Smash TV out of Limbo. Any enjoyment from that idea is quickly dispelled thanks to its unpleasant and obnoxiously difficult gameplay. It’s strange, because everything else almost works. The music is great at setting the tone, the landscapes aren’t dull, and the premise has potential. Any problem with A Quiver of Crows involves its unengaging gameplay. I kept dying constantly, but I never felt compelled to overcome my obstacles. Sometimes I won, sometimes I lost, I didn’t care that much either way. I lost all desire to see the end after a couple hours of play. Maybe I’m just a scrub, but I’d prefer to have fun when getting my♥♥♥♥♥kicked.
FULL REVIEW:

My reservations about AQOC could be potential resolved but I have to give a no for now.
One of the biggest complaints I have with the game is the respawn rate of enemies, which was, at time of playing, a nightmare. There were certain levels where I had a better chance of beating the level if I speedran them than if I actually took the time to clear out a room, because the clearing out would just never happen. Enemies would keep pouring in as soon as I dealt with the existing enemies around me. It was often relentless and neverending. That relentness can be good in a twin-stick shooter but it has to have a reasonable end point.
Especially when taking any damage reduces the effectiveness of your weapon, which has a snowballing effect against you. I couldn't really tell what playstyle was meant to be rewarded in this game. Careful? Aggressive? Speedy? I don't know.
The art and music are alright, the sound is a little weak and lacks oomph, but none of that detracts from the gameplay. The gameplay itself I think would be fine and the setting unique and quirky if it wasn't such a test of endurance.

This is a game for those who like tinkering with systems and enjoy building the best designs. Think of the old adage "try to build the better mouse trap" The game itself is simple, design ships, face off against an array of enemy's and win. What this game does though to is credit or determent, depending on who you ask. Is that you must make all your plans and strategies before you even warp in.
No there is no way to directly control your fleet in battle. This game is pure macro management and completely cuts out micro. This is done for fairness in facing off agings other players fleets. Which is the main part of the game once you beat the main mission chain. The fact that since the opponent can only set guidelines for their fleet before they upload it is only fair that you must do the same as well.
The challenge and what makes this game have a high replay value is that you must build your fleet on a budget. Each match has a max number of points "Honor" that you can spend and what you don't spend you earn in points at the end of the match provided you win. These points are then spent to unlock items like weapons, parts and new ship hulls including bits and bobs that you can use in the editor. You however can only earn that extra honer once and to earn more you must beat the challenge again with a smaller fleet.
The big new thing over this sequel is the ship editor. This allows you to truly make your own fleet. Form the base hull you can then add items to it to allow for a large range looks. Make your own race or try to remake your favorite SciFi franchise.
Also in this game modding is built in and fully supported. Adding new components is vary simple so long as you have the software to make the part and their is the full workshop integration that makes the steam version truly shine.
As of the writing of this review there are some stability issues that are being worked on by the team and updates are frequent. There are also a number of things about the interface and how things are done that can be improved. And personally the support from the developers is really great and fast.
For what the game offers the current price of 29.99USD may be a bit steep for most. Considering that there should be a good amount of DLC if the first game is any indication.

It took a while for me to get into this game. The first chunk of time I spent on it left me awfully stuck, and I had quite a few moments where everything felt hopeless and I didn't know what to do. I ended up consulting a walkthrough to get me back on the right track. But once I got on that track, it felt like everything fell into place really nicely.
I think one of my biggest qualms with this game was that it was incredibly difficult to get a feel for the arrangement of the different locations. I found myself constantly wandering back and forth between areas because I just didn't know what options led me where. I think this game would have really, really benefited from a map feature. Just to be able to clearly visualize how the different areas were connected would have probably solved all of my issues.
That being said, the prose in this game is lovely, and the ending made it worth it for me. Even after I got stuck a lot, the way the plot worked out in the end was really satisfying from a storytelling point of view. 7/10 from me.
(A side note--maybe a glitch? Every time I exited out of the game, I had to recollect all the items I previously collected. They were lit up in my inventory, but I had to physically go back to the places I found them and go through the dialogue to collect them again. I thought the game automatically saved, and even though when I restarted it, it put me where I left off, the items I had needed to be collected again. Strange.)

is a piece of interactive fiction in which the player explores and uncovers the story of a fictional European city set around the time of the First World War. The author tries to add quality to the story by romanticizing every sentence, which, in opinion, feels excessive and simply makes the reader lose interest. The narrative feels more like it is trying to describe the architecture of every building in the city rather than to describe the events that should make up the bulk of the storyline. There is very little sound in the
, the reader can only experience music when the
option is selected, the rest of the time the user being in total silence, which is a disadvantage in the case of interactive fiction.
In my opinion this digital story doesn't belong on Steam, it isn't captivating enough to maintain the reader interested and the lack of a background soundtrack just maintains the reader in dull silence. The only reason I didn't uninstall it the moment I lost interest is that it gave me the first achievement when I activated the storyline and I decided to consult a guide to get the last 2 achievements. 4/10

Enter a realm in which mortals played gods, and ultimately failed.
The graphics aren't surprising, and they are standard - but they are even in their "enlarged" state not ugly and not unsightly.
Quite standard fare for a RPGMaker game. Nothing outstanding, but also nothing too annoying.
The game has some traps laid out, but those actually make the game work perfect in all other areas. The traps are, spots were a low level character can get killed too easily... so take care, and play through the game. I encountered no bugs... some minor typos and a game that ran smoothly and without even once crashing - and I tried hard to get it crashing... No chance at this. You can't save everywhere in the game which actually isn't bad at all. And encounters are often visible on the maps (only not on the world map).
Genre Values:
You play Arres a Battlemage with no history at all, and as shrouded as your history is your future and your abilities. You start off trying to know more about your surroundings, and you learn about the monsters invading all the lands - and about the labyrinths which were created by the four elemental gods. The story is well executed, not too nosy and you choose the pace in which you will do your duties.
You don't gain powers automatically by rising up a level or by just grinding enough monsters to gather EP's you have to search and look for your powers and it is easy to lose track of powers or even imagine what powers there are in the game for you. This is good, since some spells open up new tactics and new possibilities to get your foes more readily vanquished.
Though the game has simple graphics, you can lose yourself in the game. I started to play it and suddenly five hours were gone - most of this effect is derived from the nice story of the game. You just want to know what is your next step, where to go next - why are the people of one city so damn aloof, while in another town you are taken in with a lot of respect. The story uncovers over time your own story, and this makes the game a nice experience. Even grinding is by far not as enervating as you might expect.
Alone on this I can say that I was positively surprised by the game, first it's under one buck to buy the game. Depending on how forced you play it, you might solve the game in between 10 to 20 hours, a lot of tripple A games with a lot of fancy graphics but a bad storyline offer less to a much higher price, or spread their contents over several editions of the game. The game isn't the invention of the tyre, but it is decent, nice to play and offering some neat entertainment.
The game offers at least 10 hours of game time, a good story and stable gameplay, all this for a really low price.
As I said, the gamedeveloper didn't invent the tyre new, but he tried to deliver a game that runs without killing your time in waste. The only thing that troubled me was the story between Arres and Ann... Huh? You wan't to know? Buy the game... NOW... You'll see it's fun, especially to read the awkward situation between the Hero and his Heroine... maybe a bit cheesy... but still fun. ***Remark: No cheese was harmed during writing this Review***

I was initially very excited to play this game, it completely enticed me. The concept, though based on the Wizard of Oz and other fairy tales, was creative and cute. They even added the concept of the mafia into it. It seemed interesting enough so I bought it and played it.
I was disappointed for several reasons. Not to say that this game is bad, it was enjoyable and cute, but it has flaws.
I've only completed one character route, but I don't think I'll play the others. The plot is a bit lacking. I checked other reviews, and there is a plot, but when you're playing the game, it feels like you're just playing through choppy movie cutscenes that start and end abruptly. The beginning of the game was alright, with the music intro and exposition. I thought OZMAFIA!! was a Japanese game translated to English and released on the market, becuase the the artwork is brilliant and beautiful and because of the music opening. The exposition could have been better though. It felt a bit too rushed. What script the game has is well written with few grammatical errors and typos, (though I did find some), but I wish the developers added more. It would help with the plot holes and the "choppy" scenes.
Another reason I was disappointed was the voice acting. When I bought the game, I thought it was fully voiced, but this is not the case. The beginning is voiced but towards the middle and end, the voice acting starts getting choppy because only certain lines are voiced since the developers of the game added more script after the voice acting was done. For $34, I expected full voice acting.
The final reason I was disappointed was the quality/resolution of the game. I played on both Windows and a Macbook with retina display. I expected the quality on retina display to be better. The game, even in full-screen mode, does not fill up the entire screen for either Windows or Mac. There are several inches cut off from the sides and though the art is beautiful, it is pixley. I understand that OZMAFIA!! is the developer's first otome game, but I wish they could make the game at least fill up the whole screen.
The game has a high replay value since it's an otome game, but the common route would get tiring after a while. The only new parts of "story" the game has, after your first playthrough, happen when you choose who you want to spend time with on Sunday. This makes the script even more choppy.
Overall, I did enjoy the game. I don't regret spending my money, but I wish the game was . . . better. I wish the developers good luck in their future games. This dones't make the game bad, but I didn't really like the personality of the female protagonist, but this is just in my opinion as some people will like her and some will not.

Inventory managment is a key element to survival. Combining health items to create greater health items. Needing to open your inventory to equip a weapon, much like opening a bag to retrieve something in real life. With certain characters having larger inventories with certain restrictions. Making team work and item managment vital to survive.
Your characters are not action heroes. They are quite frail and in the hands of a new player are unlikely to survive. An experienced player can avoid trading hits. But until you are used to the controls and how the enemies behave. You're likely to be forced to trade hits in melee. Making ranged weapons very valuable. Wasting a bullet can mean the difference between success and failure. Your chances are even lower if your friends don't communicate and share.
As of 8/23/2017 the game is still in a very early state. Animation and graphics need polish. Some of the gameplay mechanics are a little rough. But overall it's a very good start. Online play works very well with a cloud based network that avoids NAT problems with Peer 2 Peer connectivity. Just make sure you're all on the same cloud server and it should work just fine.

Simple jigsaw puzzle game that somehow gets it wrong.
I like both digital and physical jigsaw puzzles. I'm not spectacular at them or anything but I enjoy them. Guess I'm a boring dude! Needless to say I figured this game would occupy me for a few hours and be worth the trade I made for it. But it suffers from a some flaws.
The difficulty curve is non-existent;
Beyond piece count increasing there's no challenge. There is no piece rotation so each piece is always in it's correct orientation. Then the way some puzzles are "cut" the pieces are TOO unique and spotting a pair is a breeze. Pieces lock to their place on the board so any time you're stuck you can drag and drop around until you get "lucky" if you're really determined to get rid of a piece. But pieces will not lock to each other freely outside of their spot on the board, so there's no putting together a few pieces out of place and moving them all together into place later.
Interaction and interface is um weird;
You have your build space but no open space to pre-build (not that you can anyway like mentioned above). All the "loose" pieces are floating in a upside-down L-shaped koi pond and they are constantly floating around and moving. And there, I swear to you, lurks a little gremlin of monumental proportions! And it isn't the koi fish... You can't see him but I swear to you he is there. No matter what. I dunno how the game does it. But no matter what. The piece you want to click to pick up will NEVER be the piece you want if there's another piece remotely close. It is absolutely uncanny. I actually get excited when I get a piece I was actually trying to snag, that's how rarely it happens. I thought it was just with edges, that it didn't like edge pieces, but nope. There's a effin' gremlin in there mocking me and making my mouse click pick up anything but the piece I want. This issue gets more and more ridiculous as the amount of pieces increases. The koi pond stays the same size and more and more pieces go in it as you get to later puzzles. pieces will begin to overlap four or more deep in later puzzles. And the gremlin will just laugh at you.
Then there's the normal small dev team stuff you could normally overlook;
-Puzzle pieces in the koi pond are much smaller than on the board creating visual discrepancies.
-When you "drop" a piece back to the pond it doesn't go where you drop it, it goes to a specific starting point in the middle of the action. So you cannot attempt any organization of pieces.
-Sound settings made in main menu don't save to in-game. I wanted music off and SFX on. But then in-game its just everything off or everything on.
-Messed with windows 10 title bars when played fullscreen and minimized to desktop.
-Always launches in fullscreen even if you switched to windowed last play.
-No saving mid-puzzle.
-Etc.
Just can't recommend it. At any price.

Computer puzzle games have been around for a long while – well as far as I can remember. My earliest knowledge is called ‘European Scene Jigsaw Puzzles Vol. 1’ by Thorn EMI UK way back in 1981.  A nice game with crisp graphics amid the moderate choice of colours, it served its purpose. Fast forward to April 2014, another puzzle game caught my attention which happens to be in the form of this review – Pixel Puzzles: Japan. What attracted me to this game is the theme (Japan) that plays upon the ‘traditional’ puzzle gameplay. Well, once I have knocked out all the puzzles, this puzzle game leaves a lot to be desired.
So let’s start off with the good points first. This puzzle game certainly does have a traditional Japanese feel with the puzzle borders filled with water and floating Lilly pads – that is the Koi Pond. Also there’s a carp swimming about where you can actually can catch it. Place the carp on the puzzle board and he’ll fishtail back (excuse the pun) to the pond. There are other things you can do to the carp however I let you discover it (and no, you cannot eat it).
There are nineteen puzzles to choose from and the pieces range from sixty to the granddaddy three hundred and fifty. I guess the puzzle purists won’t considering three hundred and fifty large however, in this game, it’s the largest. The puzzle pieces are not your ‘traditional’ piece as most have weird shapes to them. In addition to this, you cannot refer to the puzzle picture at all as there’s an additional ‘feature’ where you need to unlock - the ‘Power of the I-Ching’.
The way this works is that there’s a golden ‘Yin Yang’ piece randomly placed in the puzzle. Once you place the piece on the random placement, you unlock one part of the I-Ching. Do this eight times you can use its power. The power is the reveal the actual picture for a short moment or two and that’s about it. Talking about a buzz killer aye. I guess the developers needs something ‘authentic’ to enhance this game.
And now here comes the unpleasant parts. First thing is this I-Ching concept – personally it’s just a waste of feature as the puzzles are all quite easy to do. Granted some are a little difficult however for me, the I-Ching is just a gimmick that can do without. Secondly, you can go crazily clicking on every part of the canvas until the piece slots in as there’s no penalty to do so. Also, because the game forces the pieces to slot in nicely, it takes away the fun of building ‘mini canvases’ all over the board.
Third, you cannot rotate the pieces so every piece is the right way up so it’s making this easy puzzle game even easier to play. Fourth, there’s no save feature so you cannot park the puzzle to take a little rest and fifth, there’s a bug where, when you try to grab a puzzle piece from the pond, there’s a good chance that you will select another piece close to it instead of the one you have chosen. I think the reason behind this is the puzzle's algorithm. It’s designed that, if there’s a couple of pieces bunched up together, the algorithm selects the piece that represents the north western corner of the picture first and finally, south eastern corner last.
Yet there’s two more that really grips me the most. The first being the quality of all the pictures. I presume they are the developer's photos however, all the pictures are extremely low quality. This is an absolute no-no as, being a puzzle game, its primary objective is to provide the user high quality pictures. The second is the abysmal sounds – the background music is nothing more than a short musical scores that loops over and over again. Also the sound quality, just like the photos are abysmal – very low quality; so low you can even hear the hissing sound. At least they could have bought a decent microphone or maybe remove the hissing sound from the original recording.
Other than completing the puzzles, there’s an extra feature where you can view the gallery and see who made this game (without the dart board). There’s also two additional puzzles to complete at any time as, I believe are the free DLC for this game – another words, you don’t have to unlock them. So being a ‘traditional’ puzzle game is nothing more than a farce. With so many negatives, it’s a wonder why I completed all the puzzles. Actually the main reason why I did is because of the achievements. If there wasn’t any, this puzzle game will be ditched straight into the bin, figuratively speaking.
3 / 10

Pixel Puzzles has beautiful pictures and soothing music, but for a jigsaw game, it is lacking: the tiles are not customisable and you cannot use your own pictures or music. At least it is cheap and has Steam integration.
Jigsaw video games are simple stuff. All you need is a decent algorithm for the tiles, good-looking pictures, and some customisation options. Pixel Puzzles: Japan meets the first two criteria and completely misses the third.
The theme is Japan, so the pictures show the best tourist traps that country can offer, with some traditional (but still Western audience compatible) music in the background.
As the game progresses, the number of tiles per picture increases, along with the variety in edge shapes. The tile design for the most part is acceptable, although in later stages the small ones can be problematic.
While the initial 18+2 puzzles are nice, they are also the entire content: you cannot add own pictures, cannot even modify the setup of the original ones… the player has no control, therefore, the game has zero replay value. Which in a jigsaw game is probably the biggest drawback that can ever be.

I'm very bad at writing a review, so I'll just point out pros/cons facts about the game:
Pros:
-Stunning scenery -I have probably never seen a sandbox game with better scenery. Climb a nearby mountain and just look around the entire world! The visibility is pretty much endless, but you need a good PC to enjoy everything on high details.
-Visuals and details -From mere statues to exploring dark tombs using a torch, everything looks awesome. As is usual in AC series, you get a lot of historic information from tombs and papyruses.
-Long gameplay -I think it took me around 40 hours just to complete the main story, although I was doing a lot of sidequests and playing on Nightmare mode. 100% completion took me 66 hours.
-"God" mode -Finally you don't feel like a god. This is what I always hated on AC games. Unfortunately the combat system is a bit clunky as I will describe it in cons section.
Cons:
-Quests -There is literally only ONE original quest. The rest is either assassinating some guy, killing a bunch of bandits, eradicating a few beasts, or rescueing someone. The worst thing is that pretty much every quest use the same formula, so there is nothing unexpecting. To top it all, allies can't die, so rescueing missions are a joke. Where are tailing missions? Minigames? Destroying stuff? Quests are simply boring, very similar and disappointing.
-Things to do -The worldmap is huge, yet the variety of actions you can do there is very small. Surely the devs could come up with more things to do than just clearing bandit/Roman camps, opening about million chests and climbing on top of pyramids and other structures.
-Combat system -Finally it's pretty much impossible to fight several enemies at once as you will die quickly. Unfortunately this is mainly due to a bit unfair combat mechanics. Some enemies have a really stupid combos that can pretty much insta-kill you. Shields sometimes work, sometimes not, enemy archers have an insane autoaim and to top it all, you can't heal during combat unless you have weapons with special perks, or if you go hide and wait for a while (but you will only recover 1/3 of your health).
-Progress tracker -I have no idea why this AC game have no progress tracker. IIRC, all previous AC games have it.
-Music -The music is not bad, but it's quite forgettable and it doesn't really capture the Egyptian atmosphere imho. I miss the music from Jesper Kyd. I'm pretty sure Ubisoft could hire many artists that would do a better job than Sarah Schachner (anyone remember the soundtracks from Pharaoh or Children of the Nile?)
-Dying -There is no penalty for dying, so in some cases it's actually faster/better to just let yourself die. You won't even fail a quest. That is a bad gameplay mechanics.
Me rikey.

*Spoilers*
At the end of the game, you are forced to assassinate Caesar, who is portrayed as an evil tyrant, and ally with the treacherous cowards Brutus and Cassius who are portrayed as heroes.
In truth, Caesar was a champion of the people. Brutus and Cassius did not fight for freedom as the game implies. They killed Caesar because they wanted power of their own, and the only way they knew how to get it was to ride on the back of a great man and then literally stab him in the back, betraying everything he built. Before his death in the senate chambers, the game shows Caesar boasting about his divinity and saying he is a god, even though Caesar never thought of himself as a god. It then shows Brutus condemning Caesar for this, even though after Caesar's death, Brutus put his face on Roman currency which was previously an honor reserved to gods and the deceased.Thankfully, in real history, Brutus and the rest of the corrupted senate were put down by Caesar's adopted son, which makes the ending to origins be even more nonsensical because it ends up being entirely pointless. They kill a "tyrant" in order to restore"freedom", yet  Rome forms into an empire anyway? The game was right to show Ptolemy and Pompey as villains, yet putting Brutus and Cassius on a high pedestal is blatantly hypocritical and incredibly stupid.
Aside from its inaccurate portrayal of many historical characters, Origins struggles with morality as well. The game constantly lectures the player on a whole slew of subjects, none of which it seems to be able to make its own mind up on as they are constantly contradicted throughout the game. One minute, you'll be playing a quest that lectures you on greed and the sanctity of the deceased, then five minutes later you'll be sacking an ancient tomb for loot. There's a small quest chain where you kill Roman soldiers for hunting animals, even though you've hunted hundreds of animals at that point. Once you finish that quest, there's literally a quest right next to it where you rescue a Roman hunter who's being attacked by lions, 30 SECONDS after you slaughtered dozens of hunters for the same thing! There also is not a single point where you can make a decision about anything anywhere. Not in the main quest, not in any of the side quests, not anywhere. The whole game forces you down a linear path of skewed morality that's so confusing the game itself doesn't even understand it.

Where to  begin with this hidden, deeply moving, rare little gem? Most people will not consider it a game at all, but I couldn't care less. This is a  well-informed piece of fictional writing, drawing on late 19th-, early 20th-century history, crafted carefully upon myriads of intertextual connotations and historical references. Consider it an exercise on creative writing, rather than a text adventure, although the structure of the story has been worked out enough to make it functional as a game, too.
You will experience the solitary exploration of a dark, forgotten city. You will get lost in empty corridors, deserted neighbourhoods, and burnt libraries. In the process, and if you are careful and receptive enough, you will also learn something about the betrayed dreams of social visionaries in the past. While doing my walkthrough I couldn't help bringing in mind Italo Calvino's invisible cities or Bilal's "town that didn't exist".
I feel really, really lucky that I came across this title, and I cannot recommend it strongly enough, at least for those steam users who can still appreciate the beauty of letting your imagination fill the gaps between the words. This is what reading and writing books is all about, isn't it? Instead of approaching it as a game that lacks entertainment, see it as a book that explores the possibilities of digital platforms. The author-developer is clearly aware of theoretical discussions on the nature of historical and popular memory and he/she made a fantastic effort to blend the two in the medium of interactive  fiction.
My only reservation (and this not on literary but rather on "gaming" grounds) is that players-readers whose native language is not English will find the prose too demanding if not tiresome. And yet the effort will pay off even at the cost of resorting to a  dictionary from time to time, as I did. After all, how  many "games" can we find around  that follow the tracks of fin de siecle radical movements,  or cite Arvo Part as an influence?

- Bertrand Russell
is an interactive fiction about a city ruined by war. You get to explore that city and ponder about the past, the present and the future set in motion by the people involved in it.
I love how well-written the story is. That's rare on a free-to-play Steam game. So kudos to the writers for writing a rich and engaging piece of adventure. The game aspect of this though is pretty awful. The choices you make are pretty linear, there are little triggers, no alternate twists and whatnot. It's really just a straightforward prose in the guise of a visual novel game. So if you find reading tedious then you might not enjoy this game. Especially since the game doesnt even have any background music to add to the mood or ambience to what you are reading. Spell boring.
Story-wise it's 7/10.

This is not just a redo of GSB1.  The game improves the graphics and the game play is similar to the original in that you design each of your ships, select and put together your perfect combination of those ships, give each ship orders for battle contigencies and then watch it unfold!   Formations of ships, placement and orders given, all play a role in what happens in the battles.  That part is the same and even better than the original!!!  GSB 2 adds new ship categories including gunships, destroyers (support ships) and Dreadnaughts (aka: battleships).  The Dreadnaughts can also be outfitted to be carriers as well.  It all depends on your designs.  This is where GSB 2 really shines!  You can modify all defensive and offensive aspects as well as engines, crew cabins, targeting enhancements, etc.  Once you decide on your ship's functional pieces and parts, you can design the asthetic pieces by adding various wings, structures, vents, engines, antennae, and so much more!  Pick the color of your ship and/or each individual part.  You can add spinning, blinking, and glowing parts to your ships.  So MANY choices! --The possibilities are nearly endless.  The battle modes are fun with 3 different levels of difficulty.  If that is not enough action for you, then try my favorite part, the "CHALLENGES"!  Face other players' fleets in asynchronous battles online.   The extra Steam workshop features push this game over the top.  If you are new to this, then the workshop can help you even more, being able to see what others are doing with their ships, etc.  I have spent many hours on the 1st game, the beta of this one, and will spend MANY more hours (much to the chagrin of my wife)  on this one!  This is NOT an arcade-style ACTION game.   It is not a 4X game.   It is an intellectual, planning and creative game that will provide hours of enjoyment as you try to build a better fleet than the game's or other players on the internet!

Unlike GSB 1, where there wasn't much in terms of ship class specialization, GSB 2 is all about specializing what a ship can do based on its size.  This means that each ship size only has a few different weapons/modules, and they all basically do the same thing.  Dreadnaughts, for example, have a handful of different laser and missle weapons they can use.  But the range is the same on just about every component, and the damage is very similar.  Ultimately your choice comes down to "fire slightly faster or hit slightly harder".  There also isn't really a good point defense option in the game either, but that doesn't really matter because missles are just basically slow beam weapons - they lack the range or damage or GSB 1 missles weapons.
Like I said, GSB 2 predicates the game on specializing ships based on size.  Dreadnaughts are *supposed* to have a hard time killing fighters, which are supposed to be good at killing dreadnaughts, for example.  The idea behind this is you need a mix of fighters/destroyers/dreadnaughts to have a viable fleet.  In practice this specialization doesn't work.  Fighters can't damage dreadnaught shields or armor, and dreadnaughts have access to tractor beams which allow them to kill fighters.  Destroyers meanwhile, which are supposed to be the anti-fighter ship, arn't amazing at killing fighters because destroyers are quite fragile and, unlike dreadnaughts, fighters actually can kill destroyers quite quickly.  The AI is kind of stupid and ignores destroyers with its fighters, but that doesn't fix the underlying problem.
Ultimately, I found that a fleet composed of dreadnaughts, each of which had two tractor beams, could easily beat all of the normal and hard missions in the game.  The absolute lack of components makes this a very boring strategy, as just about every ship of a given class is going to look almost identical to any other ship of that class regardless of how you try to build it.
I was also dissapointed with the other races.  The game ships with 4, the basic terran race you get at the start and the 3 other races that you have more than enough points to unlock after the tutorial mission (along with just about every component, seriously I know I said this before but I think I had unlocked literally everything by mission 4).  I don't get what the benefit of the other races over the terran race is.  They all appear to be the same - focused very heavily on armor with 1 or 2 exclusive components that arn't really any different from the basic components.  One thing I really liked about GSB 1 was that the races were quite distinct, but GSB 2 is just really lacking in that area.
All in all, the game is dissapointing.  I see what they were going for design wise - trying to force you to make more complicated fleet and ship designs by hyper specializing each ship class.  However, their implementation of that fell flat on its face and, in practice, all it has led to is a very simplified, very boring version of GSB 1.

VERDICT: Pixel Puzzles: Japan is a well-made game that provides a good if quite not complete simulation of jigsaw puzzle-solving on a PC.
There are a good number of puzzles to solve, with a fair variety of pictures. Each one using a nice mix of colours and joins
to keep the challenge fresh and the puzzle-solving experience interesting.  While the learning curve may about right for casual players the overall difficulty is pretty easy. Even the hardest puzzle is just a question of applying time, patience and perseverance to reach the final solution. Probably the only thing missing is that pieces cannot be rotated which though significant isnt really an issue.
I enjoyed it. Its not my sort of usual game but its relaxing enough to while away some time between larger more complex or action-oriented games. If you have ever received a physical jigsaw puzzle and enjoy solving them then you will enjoy the challenge the game provides even if it is not a complete representation. If you have never tried solving puzzles in real-life then this may be ideal for you to try and see if you like it.
01. GENRE: Casual Jigsaw Puzzle Simulation.
02. SETTING: Japan themed pictures.
03. STORY/BACKGROUND: n/a.
04. GAME MODES: Single-player. As its name implies the game allows you to play (make) twenty-one unique jigsaw puzzles of various sizes and difficulty, with themed pictures from one of my favourite cultures - Japan. Smaller puzzles those with fewer pieces must be completed in order to progress to harder ones those with more pieces.
05. GAME/LEVEL DESIGN: Overall the design is spartan with the only focus being to complete the puzzle. The makers have included almost all the few facets required to keep jigsaw-puzzle solving great fun and the range of pictures ensures boredom wont set in.
06. GAMEPLAY/MECHANICS: The aim is of course easy enough.  Rearrange the pieces to complete the original picture.  Playing pieces are cut differently between most pictures. You can call upon a picture reveal feature to receive hints in-game. Different joint designs ensure that players will not get used to one style of grooves which keeps playing fresh.
There is no mid-game saving unfortunately. Which is not a problem with the smaller puzzles but if you want to take a break during an attempt on the larger puzzles you will need to complete it or restart from scratch.
Pieces of the jigsaw cannot be rotated, so this makes solving them a little easier. Even if the addition of a 'stream' to keep the pieces moving was added to replace this, it makes picking up pieces that much more fiddly. To the point that it becomes fairly annoying when after five or sixe tries on the larger puzzles, you cannot pick up the piece you want.
07. ENEMIES: N/a.
08. A.I: N/a.
09. CONTROLS: Mostly its a question of mouse-driven point and drag. Letting go where you wish to place the current selected piece. Moving the cursor over the piece that you wish to select isnt as straightforward as you would imagine. Especially with the constant movement of all pieces in the stream. Though strangely, this seems to be an intended 'feature' not a bug. Likely something to replace the lack of rotating pieces which you would get in RL.  At least when a piece is dropped there is a nice sounds to inform players that it has been placed on its correct position.
10. GRAPHICS: Decent well-drawn/computerized pictures and portraits of Japanese themed subjects. Nothing amazing but more than adequate.
11. SOUNDTRACK & AUDIO: A melodic Japanese themed score that chimes along at an apt rate in keeping with the slow methodical way in which many players (I expect) will be attempting to solve their puzzles.
12. VOICE ACTING: N/a.
13. CHALLENGE/DIFFICULTY: Fairly easy. Especially the first few puzzles. There are a few harder ones providing more of a challenge later in the game.  Plus the variation in joint design adds to the problem solving as progress is made.
14. PROBLEMS: Picking up intended pieces as they are constantly moving in the stream. Though as explained this likely a feature with a non-pinpoint mouse cursor. I was also unable to capture screenshots using the Steam overlay.
15. ACHIEVEMENTS: Easy to complete. Almost all are triggered on solved the puzzles available in game. A further two are quick fun interface achievements.
16. DLC: None. There are other games in the series that use other themes if you want more of the same.
17. MODDING/ONLINE PLAY/COMMUNITY: N/a
18. ENJOYMENT/APPEAL: Anyone who like solving jigsaw puzzles and has a computer will enjoy it. Bonus if you like all things Japan.  IF you are a lover of hardcore or action games you may best our time on other games!
19. PLAYTIME/LONGEVITY/REPLAYABILITY: I suppose if you dont mind replaying the puzzles over and over you could potentially play this infinitely or at least many many times. Otherwise there is a good 10h+ if you are just happy to play through each puzzle once and only once.
20. VALUE FOR MONEY: Great on a sale. I wouldnt necessary recommend it at full price though it depends, on how many times you intend to replay the puzzles. Personally I don't feel the retail price offers value for money unless you aim to replay the puzzles every so often. As this is the first in the series unless you are put off by the Japanese theme or prefer one of the other titles (Zombie, Birds or Anime...) I suggest you pick this up in a a sale.

I feel slightly conficted on this game. I like the visuals, controls and puzzle aspect of DeadCore, but I don't like the emphasis on trying to complete levels as fast as possible and flawlessly. It feels like if Portal 2 had less thinking involved, a ton more cognitive coordination required, and an emphasis on speeding through each level.
Something else rather critical to point out: there's not really a story from what I've seen so far. Basically there's nothing to motivate you to complete the game beyond just for the sake of beating it. The bare gameplay mechanics are not enough for me to keep coming back to complete it.

I enjoy games with simple mechanics and an emphasis on speedrunning. But this game suffers from the same issues as Cloudbuilt in that it is far too complex. I only managed to get up to level 4 and I gave up half way through it because rather than offering lots of small simple levels, the levels are vast and complex and a nightmare to navigate. It is not easy (at least for me) to find which way to go as there are lots of paths. There are also far too many environmental death traps to navigate. By the time you get to level 4 it's no longer about being quick, but actually just getting through the game. Where Cloudbuilt fails because of its complex environments, extreme pace and many enemies, it at least manages to keep levels short and makes it clear that being fast is what's important. Deadcore, on the other hand, fails because it offers collectibles and long levels. The only thing that makes it remotely apparent that this is a speedrunning game is the timer on your weapon. I'm not sure if I misunderstood the game, but it seems to be that this is more of a "deathtrap navigation puzzle" game than one in which you are under time pressure; at least in the first run. The core mechanics are very promising, as is the general aesthetic and design. But it suffers from complexity which makes it difficult to enjoy and recommend.

I want to start this review by stating that:
1* I've been playing a huge amount of visual novels. Ones made from actual known developers and ones from small time developers.
2* I've also played a lot of games from PlayStation 1-4.
3* I don't just write reviews for games. In fact, this is the first time I actually decided to write one for a game.
Let me discuss what you'll find in the game..
**Amazing visuals. From the Character design to the background.
**Pleasing Soundtrack.
**It's not fully voiced over but half, if not majority, of the time it is. The japanese voice acting are well done.
**They have many characters.
**Each character, despite having a lot of them, they have their own individuality. They have rich personalities I must say as well.
**With that said, there are multiple routes to choose from and each has their own respective endings.
**The Heroine has a wonderful character. Even with her memories gone, she does well in the game. Then again, this still probably depends on the player.
What made me write this review is that I fell in love with all the characters. Not just with the Oz, who seem to be the main casts, but also those of other groups. Every conversation makes me laugh and love them even more. There are other visual novel that makes me laugh of course, but this one feels different.
The story is not exactly 'romance-driven.' There IS the presence of romance in the game. You can't take that away; it is an Otome Visual Novel. But to me, in my eyes, this game shows more of the interaction of the characters to each other.
To those who read this review, hope this helps you to decide whether you'd buy the game or not.
I think it is worth the expense.

The story and setting are uninspired and underdeveloped. You are given a task and that's what you get. You can find some lore books to read that attempt to flesh out the world like what has been seen in the Elder Scrolls series, but there is nothing within the game to connect that lore, so it doesn't even matter and isn't worth the time. In terms of gameplay, it is the barebone standard of turn-based RPGs.  Having one character for more than half the game makes some status effects game ending cheap shots. Instead of having magic be a level-based unlock, there is a gimmicky cue system where you must find strange things in your environment to interact with to learn new spells. It is very unnecessary and a pain when new party members finally join for you will be off backtracking to all the areas you visited that had cues you couldn't use. Considering each area is rather small and cues being blatantly obvious, what little exploration is there is forced and uninteresting.
The graphics and sound are fine for what they are and I love pixel art, especially where RPGs are concerned. I don't personally care about stock assets considering the price of the game is so low; I understand not everyone is a born Edward Hopper. I'm more interested in plot and setting in these regards and that is where the game ultimately failed for me.

Please kindly find my video review here:
Game-play
Gratuitous Space Battles is back again, and this sequel is a dream come true to players who enjoyed the first game.
Being famous for its vast customization and allowing the players to exert their creativity, this time, even more customization is allowed.
Being able to color and re-size the vast amount of parts and modules to mount on different ship hulls sizes and more-specialized-hulls for the construction of your space-crafts, provided great complexity and possibilities for you to spend hours just to construct your own unique ship.
With mods being available and sharing of spacecraft design through steam, there is no limit to the content of this game.
This game features the standard mission game mode, which the player will need to defeat a group of preset enemy space-crafts. The less total cost of your space-crafts deployed to tackle the mission, the more honor points you will get in-return for you to unlock more modules, equipment and factions. Again, there is no direct control over the ships during the battle. However, you can assign certain tasks and behaviors of your ships during the deployment phase.
There is also an online mode of the game, which you can tackle space-craft formations created by other players.
However, this sequel still fall short on one major problem inherited from the previous game. That is, the lack of a background story. Without a story-line to hold the game together, this game ultimately feels like a space battle simulator like the one in Ender’s Game.
Presentation
Visually speaking, the upgrade of graphics was not dramatic, but there are definitely more efforts put into the details of the space-crafts and the battlefield.
Lighting and shadow effects were also improved to help create a more realistic 2.5 dimensional environment than its predecessor.
Being able to build your dream ship is one thing, but the greatest enjoyment comes from the way it shines in action or…in total destruction.
There was also a great improvement on the user interface during the battle and players can now look at each space-craft’s status at the same time.
Although some of the icons might be a bit too large which could block the view of the battlefield, this was no doubt a welcoming improvement.
Summary
In summary, if you are interested in the previous game or being a Sci-Fi fan, there is no doubt that you will be spending hours and hours of time in this sequel.
For those that are new, it depends on whether you would value the limitless creation provided by this game over the lack of a background story.

31/07/17 UPDATE: Forest Mission FAITH added along with an Onslaught Mode for the Forest Map and new experiments mode COUNTDOWN. In FAITH you must search around for items to repair a car to escape the mission. In COUNTDOWN you must complete the mission within a set amount of time, killing zombies will add to the countdown timer but healing yourself will reduce the timer. Explosive barrels added. Forest is much smaller level than Office but makes a nice change and is much more open and atmospheric. In the FAITH mission a few puzzles have been included that must be solved in order to progress. Hopefully we will see more and more of these puzzles in future levels. The game is coming along very nicely.
11/07/2016 UPDATE: Character Progression: XP and Perk system has now been implemented. Level up all characters individually to increase certain skills and earn skill points to unlock various perks from health and damage buffs all the way to increasing your inventory slots or even starting with a magnum! In multiplayer all XP is shared so you need not worry about kill stealing. All characters level up to a max level of 25 so thats a current max of 100 levels to get upgrading! All perks can be swapped in and out, so if you buy a perk you are not stuck with it, you just un-equip the perk to get your skill points back to spend on other perks.

OUTBREAK: THE NEW NIGHTMARE REVIEW
Okay so i don't play early access games anymore, purely because the lack of content/polish puts me off so much that when the game finally releases i am already put off by it, stupid i know but there we are. So i have my own "early access rule" which my friends find very annoying and basically means avoid.
That very rule was especially emphasised when my friend asked me to check out this game. Firstly, lets just address the elephant in the room. This game is a complete Resident Evil: Outbreak knock off. But thats not a bad thing, infact its a very very good thing. Capcom have had plenty of time re-release the Outbreak series and have thus far not bothered. Its the one game me and my friends always agree should be brought back, updated, and re-released. Unfortunatley the Outbreak games came out a generation too early, i mean who the hell actually played the PS2 online!?
Anyway, soon as i looked at the game i had high hopes for the finished product. I was determined not to play the early access because i was convinced i would be put off the game by the time it is fully released, but damn you steam and your ability to gift. So my friend brought it for me so we could co-op it, so i kinda HAD to play it and boy do i like what i see!
Firstly yes, it has its issues, obviously, it is early access after all. Like the map for example, it's so annoying not being able to scroll/zoom when looking at it.
EDIT: This has been fixed in a new update.
I havent played this game by myself and i won't be playing by myself as i not a huge fan of single player games, but i am a massive fan of co-op games.
EDIT: Okay so i actually enjoy playing single player too :)
The game comes with a couple scenario modes, all of which are playable with 1-4 players.
The modes are:
Campaign Mode: Currently only two scenarios, one being tutorial and the other being the first main scenario (called Outbreak) which we got 50 minutes into before finally dying. No respawns, only one life :D
EDIT: Have completed the first main mission, takes between hour, hour and half. You cannot save game even on single player so make sure you got a couple hours spare before you start.
EDIT: Can be finished in 30 mins if you know exactly where to go and what rooms you can skip (But I have done the first scenario many times)
Onslaught Mode: Wave based scenario. My friend died early on in wave 2 but i managed to finish that wave by myself only to find my friend doesnt respawn when the next wave starts :(
EDIT: We made it to wave 12, enemies get tougher and move faster!
EDIT: Made it to Wave 23 in single-player. Single player is much easier.
and finally in a recent patch they also added an Experiments mode which look set to be variations of the main game. The first Experiments scenario is called Blackout and has us running around with nothing but a flashlight whilst trying to escape the building full of zombies during a powercut so its almost pitch black.
EDIT: Got all the way to the end but died at the last enemy!!! Nooooooooooooooooo!
EDIT: We did it. Top Tip: Save all your decent ammo for the end :D
Currently all modes are done on the same "Outbreak Scenario map" but they are currently working on the next map which looks set to have us running round the city streets (Resi 2 style!)
You can invite friends through steam or setup a public lobby if you want to play with randoms.
Currently the game has 4 characters all with different abilities:
Lydia: Starts with pistol and has extra damage resistance.
Kane: Starts with lockpick (only way to get one) but is more vunerable to damage.
Ivy: Starts with healing item, and gets a healing boost whenever she heals herself.
and Harry: (My favourite) Larger inventory space. He can hold 2 extra items but is unable to combine healing items.
There are currently 9 weapons in the game. 2 melee and 7 firearms:
Knife
Fire Axe
Pistol x 3 (Good, Better, Best)
Shotgun (Yes you can aim up for extra damage with a headshot like the original Resi's)
Assault Rifle
Magnum
and Grenade Launcher
There are currently 8 enemies in the game:
Normal zombie
Fat zombie (Takes more damage to down)
Normal zombie on fire (Possible does more damage, i'm not sure yet)
Poison zombie (poisons you)
Crawler zombie (cant headshot but move slower, must aim down to hit)
Crawler zombie on fire
Guardian (sub-boss)
Guardian on fire
Guardian (big boss, looks same as guardian but has much more health)
Not including weapons there are currently 13 supplies to collect in the game:
Pistol ammo
Shotgun ammo
Magnum ammo
Assault rifle ammo
Grenade launcher ammo
Various quest items (keys etc)
Readable books/memos (cannot be collected, only read then put back)
Painkillers (Heals a little health)
Ointment (Cannot be used by itself, must be combined with Painkillers)
Remedy (Cannot be collected, must combine Painkillers with Ointment)
Ipecac Syrup (Cures poison)
First aid kit (Fully heals health and poison) (Combine Remedy with Ipecac Syrup)
First Aid Spray (Fully heals health)
All characters with the exception of Harry can only carry 4 items so you much decide which items are most important to you. Currently there are no chests in the game so any items you don't want can be dropped on the floor where they will remain until collected again (Resident Evil Zero style)
The game supports Xbox 360, Xbox One, and PS4 gamepads in addition to keyboard and mouse. Also all buttons can be remapped.
I will be playing more and more and will keep this review updated but i have very high hopes. If you are a fan of the old school Resi's or have always wanted to play Resident Evil Outbreak with friends, grab yourself a copy. If you are on the fence about this game then i recommend you go for it, its a good laugh.
EDIT: Also the developer is very active in the steam forums. They reply often and listen to feedback. Even more active in the official Outbreak Discord channel.

I recommend this interactive story if you enjoy reading light novels. I don't recommend it to people who want to "play" a game because it's not really a game. There are elements of puzzles in here, but it's so easy to figure out, and it goes along with the story that helps you unlock more story. But this isn't the reason I'm not recommending it.
This game is pure text and clicking. There is no music, and its a 2 hour game. There is only reading. But I like that you can see the items you pick up on the right side. I don't mind the text being white on black, but I understand some people find it irritating. I feel like the black background is important just because the black helps us focus our mind more to reading what the author is trying to show us.
But here are some things I found that made it rather 'annoying,' and why I'm not recommending it: first off, my visual memory is way better than trying to "picture words," so a lot of the times I'm reclicking back and forth to the same 2 or 3 areas. I think this has a lot to do with visual memory and also UI. I understand its text based, but it's easier to see that you can go 'back' into an area if the words are on the left, or forward in an area if the next place to visit is on the 'right.' Instead of the words being on top of each other -- which is a little bit unintuitive if you're entering into a room's door, but there are words at the bottom you don't realize at first that when you click makes you go back to the previous room if that makes any sense...
I'll be honest though, the story itself can be rather difficult to follow, and I have a hard grasp of actually understanding the ending... I feel like the elements and fancy wording detract from the story -- there were areas that I felt like the background was just kinda there and some stuff made no sense and didn't connect well with the overall story. It also seemed like its based on reality in the 1900s but with advanced technology and a group of people called, "Provost" but to be honest, I don't know what the provost is even after finishing because there wasn't a clear explanation on it. There wasn't any part of it where I was like, "Oh yeah! I totally see/didn't see that coming!" This story has drama, but there's no conflict -- you're just trying to find out what happened, but I find that I don't really care for it. The only thing that kept me going to the end was, I knew the ending was near and that I wanted all the Steam completions.... I hadn't tried a visual novel since Cartoon Network's Space Ghost Coast to Coast text best game, and it was soooo long ago. But I'm definitely game to see more that are imaginatively engaging and had a bit more time put into it.
